content.text:
The **bones of the head** are mainly divided into two groups:

## 1. Cranial bones (8)
These form the **cranium**, which protects the brain.

- **Frontal bone** — forehead
- **Parietal bones** — two bones forming the upper sides of the skull
- **Temporal bones** — two bones near the ears
- **Occipital bone** — back and base of the skull
- **Sphenoid bone** — skull base, behind the eyes
- **Ethmoid bone** — between the eyes, part of nasal cavity and orbit

## 2. Facial bones (14)
These form the face, nose, mouth, and eye sockets.

- **Mandible** — lower jaw
- **Maxillae** — two upper jaw bones
- **Zygomatic bones** — two cheekbones
- **Nasal bones** — two bones forming bridge of nose
- **Lacrimal bones** — two small bones in the medial eye socket
- **Palatine bones** — two bones forming back of hard palate
- **Inferior nasal conchae** — two bones inside nasal cavity
- **Vomer** — forms part of nasal septum

## Total skull bones
The adult skull is commonly described as having **22 bones**:

| Group | Number |
|---|---:|
| Cranial bones | 8 |
| Facial bones | 14 |
| **Total** | **22** |

### Other head-related bones
Some anatomy courses also include:

- **Auditory ossicles** — 6 tiny ear bones: malleus, incus, stapes in each ear
- **Hyoid bone** — in the neck, supports the tongue; not technically part of the skull

So, depending on classification, the **head region** may include **22 skull bones**, plus **6 ear ossicles**, and sometimes the **hyoid bone**.
